Daily Mirror • 2026-10-26

CBSL reviews early-settlement charges and parate execution following borrower complaints

Supervisory focus
Banking Conduct and Enforcement
What happened

CBSL conducted thematic reviews in the first half of 2026 after receiving complaints about charges for early settlement of term loans and banks’ parate execution practices. The early-settlement review covered licensed banks and finance companies; the parate review concerned licensed banks. The report does not announce findings, sanctions or new rules.

Why it matters

Direct implications for banking conduct supervision, borrower protection and secured-loan recovery practices.

Daily Mirror ↗

Daily FT • 2026-10-27

Bank of Ceylon plans Basel III Tier 2 debenture issue of up to Rs. 30 billion

Supervisory focus
Capital and Solvency
What happened

Bank of Ceylon announced a listed subordinated debt issue opening on 3 November 2026. It proposes an initial Rs. 10 billion tranche, with oversubscription options taking the maximum to Rs. 30 billion. The planned Tier 2 debentures include non-viability write-down terms; the amount is a proposed offering, not proceeds already raised.

Why it matters

Regulatory-capital planning, loss-absorbing instruments and bank funding capacity.

Daily Mirror • 2026-10-26

Nations Trust Bank and Union Assurance renew bancassurance partnership

Banking Partnerships
What happened

Nations Trust Bank and Union Assurance announced the renewal of their exclusive bancassurance partnership. The arrangement continues the distribution of life-insurance protection products through the bank’s customer channels. The report did not disclose new financial commitments or sales volumes.

Why it matters: Bank distribution partnerships, customer product governance and bancassurance conduct.

OTHER FINANCIAL SECTOR

Other Financial-Sector Developments

Licensed finance companies and material insurance-sector news

Daily Mirror • 2026-10-26

NBFI borrower-risk indicators worsen, with Stage 2 loans up 92.1%

Credit Risk and Asset Quality
What happened

CBSL figures reported for June 2026 show that 52.4% of household borrowers at non-bank financial institutions were in high or very-high CRIB risk categories, versus 24.1% at banks. Finance-company Stage 2 loans increased 92.1% year on year, with gold-backed Stage 2 balances up 279.2%. These are risk indicators, not confirmed credit losses.

Why it matters: Household indebtedness, forward-looking credit deterioration and interconnected finance-company risk.
Source: Daily Mirror ↗
Daily FT • 2026-10-27

Fitch assigns expected A-(EXP)(lka) rating to Asia Asset Finance subordinated debt

Capital and Solvency
What happened

Fitch assigned an expected national-scale rating of A-(EXP)(lka) to proposed subordinated listed debentures of up to Rs. 3 billion from Asia Asset Finance. The company intends to use the proceeds to reinforce Tier 2 capital and support loan-book growth. The final rating remains contingent on satisfactory documentation.

Why it matters: Capital quality and market funding for a licensed finance company.
Source: Daily FT ↗

Daily FT • 2026-10-27

PDMO rejects all bids in US$ 100 million domestic dollar-bond auction

Sovereign Debt
What happened

The Public Debt Management Office rejected all bids at its 23 October domestic dollar-bond auction. The proposed issue was US$ 100 million with an option to raise up to US$ 300 million. Market participants suggested bid rates were too high, but the official notice did not provide that explanation.

Why it matters: Sovereign foreign-currency funding conditions and potential effects on domestic banks’ investment opportunities.
Source: Daily FT ↗
Daily FT • 2026-10-27

Government-bond yields broadly steady; selected 2033–2034 tenors rise

Sovereign Debt and Rates
What happened

Monday’s secondary-market trading was broadly steady across most government-bond tenors, though selected 2033 and 2034 maturities faced selling pressure and higher yields. The market was preparing for Treasury-bill and Treasury-bond auctions scheduled for 28 and 29 October respectively.

Why it matters: Interest-rate movements affect the valuation and funding conditions of banks’ Treasury portfolios.
Source: Daily FT ↗
The Morning • 2026-10-27

Sri Lanka’s exports reach US$ 13.61 billion in January–September 2026

External Sector and FX
What happened

Export earnings for the first nine months of 2026 reached US$ 13.61 billion, an increase of 5.04% from a year earlier, according to figures released by Sri Lanka Customs and estimates from the Export Development Board. September exports reached about US$ 1.69 billion, up 17.23% year on year. The nine-month total includes goods and services.

Why it matters: Export receipts affect foreign-exchange liquidity, the external balance and bank customers’ cash flows.

Daily FT • 2026-10-27

Resus Energy’s Rs. 1 billion green bond gains Luxembourg listing

Sustainable Finance
What happened

Resus Energy announced the dual listing of its Rs. 1 billion green bond on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange and its display on the Luxembourg Green Exchange, effective 19 October. The bond was originally listed in Colombo in 2025; the overseas listing expands visibility of an existing security rather than constituting a fresh Rs. 1 billion issue.

Why it matters: Development of sustainable-finance capital markets and cross-border investor access.

Macro & Systemic Context

Policy developments with a financial-system relevance

The Morning • 2026-10-27

Government adopts three-month economic forecasting amid energy-price uncertainty

Macro and Systemic Risk
What happened

A Deputy Minister said the Government is using rolling three-month forecasts to respond to energy and geopolitical price shocks while preserving fiscal buffers and export competitiveness. The report also cites slower real GDP growth of 4.2% in Q2 2026 versus 5.1% in Q1, and outlines plans for 18 industrial zones over the coming one to two years.

Why it matters: Macroeconomic shock management, inflation exposure and business operating conditions can influence bank credit risks.
Source: The Morning ↗
The Morning • 2026-10-27

SLPA report flags delayed Colombo East Terminal commissioning and revenue potential

Trade and Fiscal Context
What happened

An SLPA operational review identifies equipment, staffing and systems work outstanding at the Colombo East Container Terminal. It estimates annual revenue potential of roughly US$ 180–200 million once fully operational, not revenue currently earned, and describes a commissioning programme running into June 2027.

Why it matters: State-enterprise execution risks, trade logistics and contingent public-sector investment needs.
